title: Court found eighteen non-existent authorities in filings after a litigant used AI tools for legal research
category_definition: The system produced confident content that does not exist or does not say what it was cited as saying, and that content was relied on as genuine.
ai_materiality: The litigant's own witness statement attributes the fabricated citations to publicly available AI tools, so AI generation is admitted on the record rather than inferred. This record covers the Al-Haroun matter only. In the companion Ayinde matter heard in the same judgment, the barrister denied using generative AI and the court did not find that she had, so AI causation there is not established and is not recorded here.
source_quality_basis: Approved judgment of a Divisional Court (Dame Victoria Sharp P and Johnson J), handed down 6 June 2025 and published by the Judiciary of England and Wales, with the same text available from BAILII. Paragraph 74 records the schedule of forty five citations and the eighteen that do not exist. Paragraph 76 records the claimant's statement that the citations were generated using publicly available artificial intelligence tools. No monetary figure is recorded on this record: the GBP 89.4 million in the claim is the sum sought in the underlying dispute and is not a loss, and the wasted costs orders of GBP 2,000 each were made in the companion Ayinde matter, not in Al-Haroun.
